title: Vocabulary: types of farming and money words
competency: Use words to describe farming activities and money in your village.

keywords.def: Clearing land, farming it for a few years, then moving to new land when the soil is tired.
Keeping herds and moving from place to place in search of pasture and water.
Running a large farm, in one place, for raising cattle, horses or sheep.
Large-scale growing of cash crops such as coffee, tea or sugarcane for sale.
Growing crops and keeping livestock on the same farm.
Growing food only to feed the farmer's family, on small land, with little or no surplus.
Raising animals such as cows and goats for milk and milk products.
Growing only crops, without keeping animals.
Money left after paying all the costs.

en.text: There are many kinds of farming. Shifting cultivation moves to new land when soil is tired. Nomadic farmers move with their herds; ranchers keep animals on one large farm. Commercial plantations grow cash crops like coffee for sale. Mixed farming combines crops and animals; arable farming grows only crops. Subsistence farming feeds only the family, and dairy farming produces milk.

screens.title: Moving with the herd
screens.ask: Afar pastoralists move with their camels and goats looking for water and grass. What kind of farming is this?
screens.after: Nomadic farming: herders keep moving with their animals.

screens.title: Extended definitions
paras: Shifting cultivation: land is cleared, farmed for a few years, then left for new land until its fertility returns.
Nomadic farming: people who are not permanent residents keep moving with cows, goats and sheep.
Livestock ranching: running a large farm for raising cattle, horses or sheep.
Commercial plantation: growing cash crops such as coffee, cotton, sugarcane and tea.
Mixed farming: growing crops and keeping livestock on the same farm.
Subsistence farming: growing food only for the family, on small land, with little or no surplus.
Dairy farming: raising cows, goats or camels for milk, cheese, butter and yogurt.
Arable farming: only crops are grown on the farm.

en.text: Money words help you talk about economic activities. Income is money earned; profit is what is left after costs; an expense is money spent; a fee is paid for a service; a bonus is extra pay; a benefit is an advantage; a loss is money lost; a payment is money paid for something.

screens.title: What is left?
screens.ask: A trader buys onions for 1,000 Birr and sells them for 1,500 Birr. What is the 500 Birr?
screens.after: Profit: the money left after costs.

screens.title: Money words
paras: income: money earned. "My family's main income comes from selling teff and honey."
profit: money left after costs. "The trader made a profit of 500 Birr."
expense: money spent. "Fertiliser is the biggest expense for farmers."
fee: money paid for a service. "Farmers pay a small fee to use the grinding mill."
bonus: extra money on top of normal pay.
loss: money or things lost. "The drought caused a big loss."

A farmer's income is 8,000 Birr and her expenses are 10,000 Birr. Which word describes the result?
screens.why: She spent more than she earned: 8,000 − 10,000 = −2,000, a loss.
